source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when Yeshua{H3442} finished{H3615} speaking{H1696} all{H3605} these{H428} words{H1697}, he said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}:

one_way_hebrew: ויהי כאשר כלה... לדבר — the closing formula of Deut 31:24 and Jer 26:8 (ויהי ככלות... לדבר את כל הדברים האלה) word for word. Matthew's five great discourses each close with this Torah cadence, native in Hebrew, translated in Greek (καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν).
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״ז (Perek 107) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (26:1): לדבר] + את H.

verses.translation: Do you not know{H3045} that after{H310} two{H8147} days{H3117} will be the Pesach{H6453}, and the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} will be delivered{H4560} into the hand{H3027} of the Jews{H3064} for hanging?

greek_deviations: The Hebrew names the agents: 'delivered into the hand of THE JEWS for hanging' — Greek Matthew has only the passive 'is betrayed to be crucified,' with no agent named.

לצליבה — the execution is called a hanging-up (root צלב, the rabbinic word for gibbeting a body); at 27:22-23 the crowd's cry is יתלוהו ('hang him'), from תלה, the verb of Deut 21:22. The Hebrew text consistently describes the cross in the Torah's category of hanging; Greek σταυρόω ('crucify') is the Roman category.
translation_notes: צליבה has no biblical Strong's entry; it is the rabbinic noun for hanging up/crucifixion.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:2): יהיה] יבא G; האדם] אדם AH.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the deputies{H5461} of the priests{H3548} and the great ones{H1419} of the people{H5971} were gathered{H622} in the court{H2691} of the ruler{H5057} of the priests, whose name{H8034} was Qaiphash.

one_way_hebrew: סגני הכהנים — the segan is the Temple's own administrative title (Jer 51:23's סגנים; the סגן הכהנים of the Mishnah, m. Yoma 3:9). Greek ἀρχιερεῖς ('chief priests') flattens the office; the Hebrew uses the technical term a Temple-aware author reaches for naturally.
נגיד הכהנים — 'the ruler (nagid) of the priests': the title of 1 Chr 9:11 and 2 Chr 31:13 (נגיד בית האלהים). The Hebrew gives Caiaphas the Chronicler's title, not a transliteration of ἀρχιερεύς.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:3): קאיפש] קאיפאש A; סגני... העם] גדולי העם והכהנים G.

verses.translation: And they took counsel{H3289} together{H3162} to seize{H8610} Yeshua{H3442} by guile{H6195} and to kill him{H2026}.

one_way_hebrew: בערמה... ולהורגו — the exact legal language of Exod 21:14: 'if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile (להרגו בערמה), thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.' The Hebrew brands the council's plot with the Torah's own statute for premeditated murder — the murderer whom not even the altar shelters. Greek δόλῳ ('by deceit') translates the word but cannot carry the statute.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads ולהירגו; the scan of Howard's text reads ולהורגו, corrected here. Howard's apparatus (26:4): ולהורגו] ולהרגו BEF.

verses.translation: And they said{H559}: Let it not be on the feast{H2282}, lest{H6435} there be an uproar{H7588} among the people{H5971}.

one_way_hebrew: שאון (H7588) — the roaring of massed peoples (Isa 17:12-13, 'the rushing of nations that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters'). Greek θόρυβος is generic 'commotion.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:5): בחג] ביום החג A.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when Yeshua{H3442} was in Kfar{H3723} Hananyah{H2608}, in the house{H1004} of Simon the leper{H6879},

greek_deviations: The Hebrew places the anointing in כפר חנניה — Kfar Hananyah, a real Galilean village name (the Mishnah's boundary town between Upper and Lower Galilee, m. Shevi'it 9:2) — where Greek Matthew reads Βηθανία (Bethany). A translator working from the Greek would have written בית עניא/ביתניה; a Hebrew narrator names a Hebrew village.
translation_notes: המצורע — the metzora, Torah's own category for the scale-diseased man (Lev 13-14), whom the ointment-scene host still carries as his byname.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:6): חנניה] חנניא A; סימון] שימון ABEF.

verses.translation: a woman{H802} approached{H5066} him with a flask{H6378} of precious{H3368} ointment{H4888}, and she poured{H3332} it upon his head{H7218} while he was reclining{H4524} at the table{H7979}.

one_way_hebrew: פך (H6378) — the flask of royal anointing, and nothing else: Samuel takes the פך השמן and pours it on Saul's head (1 Sam 10:1), Elisha's servant empties the פך on Jehu's head to make him king (2 Kgs 9:1-6). A woman pouring a פך on the head is, in Hebrew, a king-making scene. Greek ἀλάβαστρον ('alabaster jar') names the container's stone and loses the coronation.
משיחה — 'ointment' from the root of משיח: the Mashiach receives mishchah on his head. The wordplay exists only in Hebrew; Greek μύρον is scentless of it.

והוא מסבה לשלחן — 'while he reclined at table': Song 1:12, עד שהמלך במסבו נרדי נתן ריחו — 'while the king was at his reclining, my spikenard gave its fragrance.' The Hebrew scene re-enacts the Song's verse — the king at his couch, the woman's perfume filling the house.

verses.translation: And it was exceedingly{H3966} displeasing{H7489} to them: Why{H4069} this waste{H11}?

one_way_hebrew: וירע להם מאד — the displeasure idiom of Gen 21:11 and Jonah 4:1 (וירע... מאד), native Hebrew narrative syntax.
אבדון (H11) — Job's word for the abyss of perishing (Job 26:6; 28:22). Greek ἀπώλεια translates the same root-idea; the Hebrew noun carries Job's shadow.
textual_notes: The transcription's footnote 148 notes the period is missing in Howard's Hebrew text here.

verses.translation: It could{H3201} have been sold{H4376} for a great{H7227} price{H4242} and given{H5414} to the poor{H6041}.

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads למוכלה; the scan of Howard's text reads למוכרה ('to sell it'), corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:9): יוכל] היה יכול B, שהיה יכול G; במחיר רב] omit G; ולתת] וליתן G.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442}, who knows{H3045} every thing{H1697} — for what matter{H6045} it was done{H6213} — said{H559} to them: Are you accusing{H816} this woman{H802}? In truth{H571} she has done{H6213} a good{H2896} and wonderful{H6381} deed{H4639} toward me.

greek_deviations: מאשימים — 'are you ACCUSING this woman?' — the Hebrew makes the disciples' murmuring a formal charge (אשם, the guilt-word of Lev 5); Greek has 'why trouble ye (κόπους παρέχετε) the woman?'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:10): לאיזה] שאיזה EF; אמר להם] אמר A; ונפלא עשתה עמדי] 2 3 1 A.

verses.translation: For the poor{H6041} will live{H2421} with you always{H8548}, but I will not be with you always.

one_way_hebrew: The clause paraphrases Deut 15:11, 'the poor shall never cease out of the land' — the very verse whose context commands open-handedness to the poor; the Hebrew reader hears the Torah text behind the saying.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads ואני לו; the scan of Howard's text reads ואני לא, corrected here.
יחיו — 'the poor will LIVE with you' (base text); mss ABEFG read יהיו ('will be'), matching the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:11): יחיו] יהיו ABEFG; העניים] העדים EF.

verses.translation: And her placing{H7760} this on my body{H1480} alludes to my burial{H6900}.

one_way_hebrew: רומז — 'hints, alludes': the rabbinic exegetical term (remez) for a meaning carried under the surface of an act. A Hebrew teacher says the deed is רומז to his burial; Greek πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ('for my burying') states the fact and loses the hermeneutical word. רמז has no biblical Strong's entry; it is the living study-house vocabulary of a Hebrew author.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you: in every place{H4725} where this good-news{H1309} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, evangel — is proclaimed{H7121} in all the world{H5769}, that which this one did{H6213} will be told in my memory{H2143}.

one_way_hebrew: בשורה זו לעז אוונגיל — the same scribal gloss as at 24:14: the Hebrew word בשורה is glossed with the church's foreign word for readers who knew it. A translator FROM Greek starts from εὐαγγέλιον and needs no gloss; the gloss runs the other way — the Hebrew word is native, the Greek-Latin word the visitor.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads אימר for אומר; the scan of Howard's text reads אומר, corrected here.
textual_notes: The transcription's footnote 149 notes that, unlike elsewhere in Shem Tov, the loanword here carries no gershayim transliteration marks (אוונגיל, not אוו״נגיל).
Howard's apparatus (26:13): זו] זאת AG; לעז] בלעז B; העולם] מקום EF; אשר עשה] omit E; עשה] עשתה ABG, omit F; בזכרי] בזכרתי A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} one{H259} of the twelve{H8147}{H6240}, whose name{H8034} was Yudah{H3063} Ashkeriotu, went{H1980} to the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548}.

textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״ח (Perek 108) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (26:14): מהשנים עשר] מי״ב תלמידיו G; ששמו] שמו FG; אשכריוטו] איסכריוטא AEF, אסכראוטה G.

verses.translation: And he said{H559}: What{H4100} will you give{H5414} me, that I should deliver{H4560} Yeshua{H3442} to you? And they fixed with him thirty{H7970} pieces of silver{H3701}.

one_way_hebrew: שלשים כסף — Zech 11:12's own wage: וישקלו את שכרי שלשים כסף ('so they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver'). The narrative states the sum in the prophet's exact words, before the text quotes Zech 11 openly at 27:9.
ויפסקו — pasak, the rabbinic verb for fixing a price or stipend; a Hebrew author's business word (no Greek behind it — the Greek has ἔστησαν, 'they weighed/appointed').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:15): שלשים] בשלשים A.
The transcription's footnote 150 notes Howard's Hebrew lacks the question mark his English carries.

verses.translation: And from then onward he sought{H1245} an occasion{H6045} to deliver{H4560} him.

translation_notes: מכאן ואילך — 'from here onward,' the standard rabbinic idiom; ענין — 'matter, occasion' (Eccl 1:13). Both are living-Hebrew usage, not calques of the Greek (ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν).

verses.translation: And on the first{H7223} day{H3117} of the feast{H2282} of the Matzot{H4682}, the disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to Yeshua{H3442}, saying{H559}: Where{H575} shall we prepare{H3559} for you the eating{H396} of the Pesach{H6453}?

one_way_hebrew: חג המצות — the Torah's own festival name (Exod 23:15; Lev 23:6; Deut 16:16), not a transliteration of Greek τὰ ἄζυμα. The community of this text keeps the feast under its Torah name.
אכילת הפסח — 'the eating of the Pesach': the idiom of 2 Chr 30:18 (אכלו את הפסח) and Exod 12:43-46, where the Pesach is a thing eaten under statute. Greek φαγεῖν τὸ πάσχα translates it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:17): ליש״ו] אל ישו ABEF; אנה] אנא BF.
The transcription's footnote 151 notes Howard's Hebrew lacks the question mark his English carries.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Go{H1980} into the city{H5892}, to whatever man{H376} whose heart{H3820} impels him{H5068} to act, and say{H559} to him: Thus{H3541} says the Rabbi: My time{H2165} is near{H7138}; with you the Pesach{H6453} will be kept{H6213} with my disciples{H8527}.

one_way_hebrew: שידבנו לבו — Exod 25:2 verbatim: כל איש אשר ידבנו לבו, 'every man whose heart impels him' — the Torah's freewill-offering formula. The householder who receives the Pesach is cast as the Tabernacle donor, moved by his own heart. Greek πρὸς τὸν δεῖνα ('to such a man') has nothing of it; no back-translator recovers Exod 25:2 from δεῖνα by accident.
כה אמר הרב — 'Thus says the Rabbi': the messenger formula כה אמר (Exod 5:1 and the prophets throughout), applied to the Teacher.
translation_notes: ויעשה פסח — the base text is impersonal/third person ('the Pesach will be kept'); mss ABEF read אעשה ('I will keep'), matching the Greek ποιῶ, and Howard's English follows the variant: 'with you (I will observe) the Passover.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:18): איש שידבנו] אשר ידבנו EF; הרב] + אדוני EF; ויעשה] אעשה ABEF.

Greek 26:19 ('And the disciples did as Yeshua had appointed them, and they made ready the passover') has no counterpart in the Shem Tov text: Howard's apparatus reads 'Vs 19] omit all mss,' and the text runs directly from v. 18 to v. 20.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} at the time{H6256} of evening{H6153}, he was sitting{H3427} at the table{H7979} with his twelve disciples{H8527}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:20): י״ב] ב״ EF.
The transcription's footnote 153 notes עם לשלחן stands in the wrong font in Howard's printed Hebrew.

verses.translation: As they were eating{H398}, he said{H559} to them: I say{H559} to you that one{H259} of you will deliver me up{H4560}.

translation_notes: כאמר — so the printed text (also the scan), apparently for כאשר ('as, while'); the sense 'as they were eating' is followed by all translators.

verses.translation: And they were exceedingly{H3966} grieved{H6087}, and every one{H259} said{H559} to him: My master{H113}, is it I?

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:22): מאד] + לאמר A; אחד] האחד מהם A; אדוני] omit EF.

verses.translation: And he answered{H6030} them: He who dips{H2881} his hand{H3027} with me in the dish{H7086} will sell me{H4376}. And all of them were eating{H398} from one{H259} dish{H7086}; therefore{H3651} they did not recognize him{H5234} — for if{H432} they had recognized him, they would have destroyed him{H8045}.

one_way_hebrew: קערה (H7086) — the Torah's dish, the silver קערה of the tribal offerings (Num 7:13ff.); Greek τρύβλιον is a kitchen word.
greek_deviations: The verse carries an explanation found in no Greek manuscript: 'And all of them were eating from one dish; therefore they did not recognize him — for if they had recognized him, they would have destroyed him.' The Hebrew answers the question every reader asks (why did no one stop Judas?) and answers it concretely: the sign pointed at every hand at the table.

ימכרני — 'he will SELL me' (מכר), where Greek has παραδώσει ('hand over'). מכר is the verb of Joseph's brothers (Gen 37:27-28, לכו ונמכרנו... וימכרו את יוסף) — the righteous brother sold for silver by his own. The Joseph typology lives in the Hebrew verb; mss AF read ימסרני ('deliver over'), assimilating toward the Greek.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads ויענ with a non-final nun; the scan reads ויען, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:23): ימכרני] ימסרני AF; שאלו] שאילו A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: Truly{H571} the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} goes{H1980} as it is written{H3789} concerning him; woe{H188} to that man{H120} for whose sake the Son of Man is delivered{H4560} — good{H2896} for that man{H376} had he not been born{H3205}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:24): בשבילו] omit G; ימסר] + בשבילו G.

verses.translation: And Yudah{H3063}, who sold him{H4376}, answered{H6030} and said{H559} to him: Rabbi, is it I? And he said{H559}: You have spoken{H1696}.

one_way_hebrew: יודא אשר מכרו — 'Yudah who SOLD him': the narrator names the deed with Joseph's verb again (Gen 37:28; cf. v. 23). Greek ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτόν ('who was betraying him') is procedural; the Hebrew is the brothers' sale.
אתה דברת — 'you have said it': the deflecting-affirmation idiom, exactly as at 26:64 (אתה אומר) and 27:11; Hebrew court speech.

verses.translation: As they{H1992} were eating{H398}, Yeshua{H3442} took{H3947} bread{H3899} and blessed{H1288}, and divided it{H2505} and gave{H5414} to his disciples{H8527}, and said{H559}: Take{H3947} and eat{H398}; this{H2088} is my body{H1480}.

one_way_hebrew: ויברך — 'and he blessed,' absolutely, with no object: the Hebrew grammar of the table-blessing (ברכת המוציא), where the blessing is addressed to God over the bread. Greek εὐλογήσας reads as if the bread were blessed; the Hebrew is the Jewish form.

ויחלקהו — 'and DIVIDED it' (חלק): David's verb for distributing the loaf to all Israel, ויחלק לכל העם... חלת לחם (2 Sam 6:19). Greek ἔκλασεν ('broke') pictures the snap; the Hebrew pictures the sharing-out from the king's hand.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״ט (Perek 109) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (26:26): המה אוכלים] omit EF; ויברך] + אותו EF, omit G; זה] זהו ABGH; הוא] omit H.

verses.translation: And he took{H3947} the cup{H3563} and gave{H5414} praises{H7623} to his Father{H1}, and gave{H5414} it to them and said{H559}: Drink{H8354} from this, all of you.

one_way_hebrew: ויתן שבחים לאביו — 'gave praises to his Father': שבח is the Psalter's loud-praise verb (Ps 63:4; 117:1; 145:4) and the Talmud's word for the table doxology. Greek εὐχαριστήσας ('having given thanks') — whence 'eucharist' — translates a Hebrew act of שבח.

verses.translation: This is my blood{H1818} of the new{H2319} covenant{H1285}, which will be poured out{H8210} for the sake{H5668} of the many{H7227} for the atonement{H3725} of iniquities{H5771}.

one_way_hebrew: ברית חדשה — Jer 31:31's own phrase (הנה ימים באים... וכרתי... ברית חדשה), the only 'new covenant' in the Hebrew Bible. The cup-word stands on Jeremiah's consonants; the earliest Greek Matthew mss lack καινῆς ('new') and later mss supply it — the Hebrew text carries what the Greek tradition wavers over.

לכפרת עונות — 'for the ATONEMENT of iniquities': כפרה is the Torah's own category (יום הכפורים, Lev 23:27-28; כפר Lev 17:11, 'the blood... maketh atonement for the soul'). Greek εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν ('for remission of sins') is bookkeeping language; the Hebrew is altar language — blood poured out to atone, exactly Lev 17:11's doctrine that atonement is in the blood.
ישפך... דם — the pouring-out of blood at the base of the altar (Lev 4:7 ישפך... דם); the verb is sacrificial in Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:28): זהו] זה הוא G; עונות] העונות H.

verses.translation: I say{H559} to you: I will not drink{H8354} from now onward from the fruit{H6529} of this vine{H1612} until{H5704} that day{H3117} when I drink it new{H2319} with you in the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: פרי הגפן — 'the fruit of the vine': the exact wording of the Jewish blessing over wine (בורא פרי הגפן, m. Berakhot 6:1). At a Pesach table a Hebrew speaker names the cup by its blessing; Greek γένημα τῆς ἀμπέλου translates the liturgical phrase without being one.
greek_deviations: במלכות שמים — 'in the kingdom of HEAVEN,' the text's fixed idiom, where Greek Matthew has 'in my Father's kingdom.' Ms A reads אבי ('my Father'), assimilating to the Greek; the base text keeps the reverent Hebrew circumlocution.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:29): אני¹] omit G; לא אשתה אני] omit B; אני²] omit EF; שמים] אבי A.

verses.translation: And they went{H1980} and went out{H3318} to the Mount{H2022} of the Olives{H2132}.

greek_deviations: No hymn: Greek Matthew (and Mark) open the verse with ὑμνήσαντες, 'when they had sung the hymn' (the Hallel). The Shem Tov base text has only 'they went and went out' — the singing clause is absent. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'when they had said thanksgiving,' agreeing with the Greek against Shem Tov.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads ויכלו ('they finished'); the scan of Howard's text reads וילכו ('they went'), corrected here — Howard's apparatus lemma at 26:30 confirms וילכו (mss ABEF read וישבו, 'they returned,' which Howard's English follows: '(They returned) and went out').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:30): וילכו] וישבו ABEF.
Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״י (Perek 110) begins at the next verse.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Come{H935}, all of you, be grieved{H6087} for me tonight{H3915}, for thus it is written{H3789}: Smite{H5221} the shepherd{H7462}, and the shepherds{H7462} will be scattered{H6327}.

one_way_hebrew: שכן כתיב — 'for thus it is written': the rabbinic citation formula (כתיב), a study-house word, not a rendering of γέγραπται.

הך את הרועה ותפוצינה — the Hebrew keeps Zech 13:7's imperative הך ('smite!' — addressed to the sword) and archaic feminine plural ותפוצינה; Greek πατάξω ('I will smite') re-voices the command as God's own future — the Hebrew stands closer to the Masoretic consonants than the Greek does.
greek_deviations: באו כלכם התעצבו עלי — an imperative: 'COME, all of you, BE GRIEVED for me tonight.' Greek Matthew has a prediction, 'all ye shall be offended (σκανδαλισθήσεσθε) because of me this night.' In the Hebrew the Master summons his men to share the night of grief; in the Greek he foretells their failure. The two sentences produce different scenes from the same consonantal skeleton of events.

The quotation ends 'and the SHEPHERDS will be scattered' (הרועים) where Zech 13:7 and the Greek have 'the sheep/flock' (הצאן). Mss AEFG read הצאן, matching Zechariah, and Howard's English prints '(sheep)'; the base ms stands alone with its plural shepherds — the under-shepherds scattered when the Shepherd is struck.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:31): אמר יש״ו לתלמידיו] אמר להם ישו ABEFGH; כלכם תתעצבו עלי] 2 3 1 F; הרועים] הצאן AEFG.
The transcription's footnote 155 confirms: mss AEFG read הצאן for הרועים.

verses.translation: And after{H310} my rising{H6965} from death{H4194}, I will be revealed{H1540} to you in Galil{H1551}.

greek_deviations: אגלה לכם — 'I will BE REVEALED to you,' where Greek has προάξω ὑμᾶς, 'I will go before you.' The Hebrew promises a revelation, not an itinerary — and it puns: אֶגָּלֶה (I will be revealed) בַּגָּלִיל (in the Galil), the same three consonants גלל/גלה rolling through both words. The wordplay is the verse's engine in Hebrew and is unreproducible in Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:32): בגליל] בהר הגליל EF.

Greek 'on the clouds of heaven' follows Dan 7:13; the Hebrew reaches instead for David's theophany psalm — the rider on the thick clouds coming to rescue the beset king. The choice of source text is itself a Hebrew author's choice.

The Hebrew answer takes up the high priest's own words (v. 63, 'if you are Mashiach the Son of El') and affirms them in the second person of the oath; the Greek deflects to the Danielic title.

לימין גבורת האל — 'at the right hand of the power OF GOD': Greek Matthew has 'the Power' absolutely (τῆς δυνάμεως); Luke 22:69 reads 'the power of God' (τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ) — the Hebrew Matthew agrees with Luke against Greek Matthew.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the chief{H1419} of the priests{H3548} tore{H7167} his garments{H899} and said{H559}: This one has 'blessed'{H1288} Elohim{H430}! What need{H6878} have we for other{H312} witnesses{H5707}? Behold{H2009}, all of you have heard{H8085} how he 'blessed'{H1288} El{H410}.

one_way_hebrew: ברך אלקים — 'he has BLESSED God': the scribal euphemism for cursing, and it is the exact charge-language of Naboth's show-trial — ברכת אלהים ומלך, 'thou didst blaspheme (lit. bless) God and the king' (1 Kgs 21:10, 13), likewise Job 1:5, 11; 2:9. The Hebrew Matthew stages the trial in the very euphemism of the Naboth frame-up: false witnesses, a capital blasphemy charge, and the word ברך where קלל is meant. Greek ἐβλασφήμησεν says the crime plainly and the allusion vanishes — a translator FROM Greek would never re-derive the euphemism.
The scene answers the Torah's statute: the blasphemy charge of Lev 24:15-16 and the garment-tearing of the horrified hearer (2 Kgs 18:37-19:1).
translation_notes: אלקים — the ms writes the reverent ק-spelling for the divine name (first occurrence in this chapter); rendered Elohim.

The transcription's footnotes 166-167 confirm ברך as euphemism, citing 2 Sam 12:14; 1 Kgs 21:10, 13; Ps 10:3; Job 1:5, 11; 2:5, 9.

verses.translation: What{H4100} seems{H7200} to you fitting{H8505} to do{H6213}? And they answered{H6030} that he is liable{H2325} to death{H4194}.

one_way_hebrew: חייב מיתה — 'liable to death': the Mishnah's own court-verdict formula (m. Sanhedrin 7:4 lists those who are חייבי מיתות). Greek ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν translates the Hebrew legal term; the Hebrew text speaks the court's working language.

verses.translation: And then{H227} they spat{H7556} in his face{H6440} and flogged him on his back{H7926}, and others{H312} slapped{H2946} him in his face{H6440},

one_way_hebrew: The verse maps onto Isa 50:6 point by point: 'I gave my BACK to the smiters... I hid not my face from shame and SPITTING (רק).' The Hebrew locates the blows on גו/שכם (the back) and the spittle on the face, as Isaiah does; Greek Matthew has generic 'they spat in his face and buffeted him.' The Servant-song geography of the abuse survives only in the Hebrew.
רקק (H7556) — the Torah's spitting verb (Lev 15:8); טפח — the slapping-out verb of Lam 2:22's טפחתי.
translation_notes: והלקוהו — הלקה, the rabbinic causative 'to flog' (the מלקות of the courts); no biblical Strong's entry. The arrest party's whips (v. 47) are now used.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:67): והלקוהו] והכוהו EF.
The circulating transcription reads הלקוהו without the conjunction; the scan reads והלקוהו, corrected here.

verses.translation: saying{H559}: Tell{H559} us, Mashiach{H4899}, who{H4310} struck you{H5221}?

greek_deviations: אמור לנו — 'TELL us, Mashiach' — Greek has 'PROPHESY (προφήτευσον) unto us, Christ.' The Hebrew mockery demands information; the Greek stages a parody of prophecy.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:68): הכך] הכה אותך G.

verses.translation: And Petros was standing{H5975} at the entrance{H6607} of the courtyard{H2691}, and a maidservant{H8198} approached{H5066} him and says{H559} to him: Were you not standing{H5975} with Yeshua{H3442} the Galilean{H1551}?

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:69): ופיטרוש] ופיטרו A; לפתח] כפתח A; אחת] omit G.

verses.translation: And Petros denied{H3584} it before{H6440} all{H3605} and said{H559} to her: Woman{H802}, I do not know{H3045} what{H4100} you are saying{H559}.

one_way_hebrew: כחש (H3584) — the biblical denial-verb (Gen 18:15, 'Sarah DENIED, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid'). The narrator alternates biblical כחש (vv. 70, 72) with rabbinic כפר (vv. 74-75) — the layered vocabulary of a living Hebrew, not the uniform output of a translator.

verses.translation: And when he passed{H5674} the gate{H8179}, another{H312} maidservant{H8198} saw{H7200} him and said{H559} to those passing{H5674} there{H8033}: This{H2088} man{H376} was standing{H5975} with Yeshua{H3442} in Natzeret.

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads עומד שם יש״ו; the scan of Howard's text reads עומד עם יש״ו ('standing WITH Yeshua'), corrected here.
בנאצ״רת — 'in Natzeret' (the transcription's footnote 168): the maid places the association in the town itself, where Greek has 'with Jesus OF Nazareth.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:71): ראה] ראהו ABEF; לעוברים] לעומדים ABEFG; עומד] omit A; בנאצרת] בנזארת A, נזארת BE.

verses.translation: And another{H312} time{H6471} he denied{H3584} Yeshua{H3442} with an oath{H7621}, that he did not know him{H5234}.

greek_deviations: כחש יש״ו — the Hebrew states it without cushion: 'he denied YESHUA with an oath' — the object is the person, not the acquaintance. Greek has 'again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.'

verses.translation: And after{H310} a little{H4592} while{H2165}, those standing{H5975} in the courtyard{H2691} drew near{H5066} to Petros and said{H559} to him: You are from the company{H2274} of this prophet{H5030}, for your speech{H4057} makes it known{H5234} that you are of them{H1992}.

one_way_hebrew: שמדברך נכר — מִדְבָּר, 'speech,' occurs exactly once in the Hebrew Bible: ומדברך נאוה, 'thy SPEECH is comely' (Song 4:3). The Hebrew Matthew uses the Song's rare word for the mouth's utterance; Greek ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ shares the sense but cannot point at Song 4:3. A back-translator would write דיבור or לשון; only a Hebrew stylist reaches for מדבר.
greek_deviations: מחבורת זה הנביא — 'from the company of this PROPHET': the bystanders name Yeshua a prophet — a title absent from the Greek of this verse ('surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (26:73): שמדברך] ומדבריך A, שמדבריך EF.

verses.translation: Then{H227} he began{H2490} to deny and to swear{H7650} that at no time{H2165} had he known him{H5234}; and immediately the rooster crowed{H7121}.

translation_notes: תרנגול — the rabbinic word for rooster (Aramaic-derived; m. Bava Kamma 7:7); the narrator uses it where v. 34 used the Mishnah's גבר. Two native words for one bird — the mark of an author at home in the language.

verses.translation: And Petros remembered{H2142} what Yeshua{H3442} had said{H559} to him, that before{H6924} the crowing{H7121} of the rooster he would deny him three times{H6471}; and then{H227} he went out{H3318} and wept{H1058} in the bitterness{H4814} of his soul{H5315}.

one_way_hebrew: ובכה במרירות נפשו — 'wept in the BITTERNESS of his SOUL': Job's phrase for the crushed man's speech (במר נפשי, Job 7:11; 10:1) with Ezekiel's noun (מרירות, Ezek 21:11 — 'sigh... with bitterness'). Greek ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς ('wept bitterly') keeps the adverb and loses the soul.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads יכפות; the scan of Howard's text reads יכפור ('he would deny'), corrected here.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 26 in the Shem Tov Hebrew tells the Passion's opening in the Torah's own legal and liturgical vocabulary. (1) 26:2 reads 'the Son of Man will be delivered into the hand of THE JEWS for hanging (צליבה)' — the Greek's agentless 'betrayed to be crucified' names no one; and the Hebrew consistently classes the cross as a hanging (cf. 27:22-23 יתלוהו), Deut 21:22's category. (2) 26:4 brands the plot with Exod 21:14's statute for premeditated murder (בערמה... ולהורגו); 26:59 seeks עדי שקר, the Ninth Commandment's words; 26:60 waits for Deut 19:15's two witnesses; 26:66 convicts in the Mishnah's formula חייב מיתה. (3) The anointing (26:6-13) happens in Kfar Hananyah (not 'Bethany'), from a פך — the royal-anointing flask of 1 Sam 10:1 and 2 Kgs 9 — of משיחה, ointment sharing the Mashiach's root, while the king reclines as in Song 1:12; the deed 'alludes' (רומז, the rabbinic remez) to his burial; and בשורה is glossed with the foreign word evangel (as at 24:14). (4) The Supper (26:26-30): he 'blessed' absolutely (the Jewish table-blessing), 'divided' the bread, calls the cup 'my blood of the NEW COVENANT (Jer 31:31) poured out... for the ATONEMENT of iniquities' (כפרה, Lev 17:11's altar-doctrine, where Greek has 'remission'), names the wine by its blessing-formula פרי הגפן, and promises to drink it new 'in the kingdom of HEAVEN' (Greek: 'my Father's kingdom'; ms A assimilates); no hymn is sung in v. 30. (5) 26:31 is an imperative — 'COME, all of you, BE GRIEVED for me tonight' — not a prediction of stumbling; the Zech 13:7 quote ends 'the SHEPHERDS will be scattered' (mss AEFG: הצאן, as Zech/Greek). (6) 26:32 puns אגלה/בגליל — 'I will be REVEALED in the GALIL' — where Greek has 'go before you.' (7) Gethsemane is native Hebrew: גיא שמנים 'Valley of Oils' (26:36), סמכוני 'sustain me' from Song 2:5 (26:38), no 'my Father' in the base text's first prayer (26:39), the flesh 'weak AND SICK' (26:41). (8) 26:52 re-speaks 1 Chr 21:27 — the sword returned אל נדנה, the destroying messenger's sheathing over Jerusalem; 26:53 claims direct power ('I am able to strike my enemies') with no prayer-to-the-Father clause. (9) The trial: Yeshua answers 'you will see the Son of EL' (26:64, where Greek has 'Son of Man') seated at the right of 'the power of EL' (with Luke 22:69 against Greek Matthew), coming בעבי שחקים — Ps 18:12 verbatim, not Dan 7's clouds; the high priest cries 'he has BLESSED God' (26:65) — the Naboth-trial euphemism (1 Kgs 21:10,13) that no translator from Greek βλασφημέω could recover. (10) 26:67 maps the abuse onto Isa 50:6 (back to the smiters, face to the spitting); the arrest party carries whips (שוטים, 26:47,55) which v. 67 uses. (11) 26:73's bystanders call Yeshua 'this PROPHET' and use Song 4:3's hapax מדבר for Peter's speech. Judas SELLS his master (מכר — Joseph's verb, 26:15,23,25) for Zech 11:12's thirty of silver, fixed with the rabbinic פסק. Verse 19 is absent from all mss; Shem Tov's section headings fall at vv. 1 (Perek 107), 14 (108), 26 (109), 31 (110), and 45 (111).
